complexity.notes: The sort is O(n log n), but each pop(i+1) shifts the tail of the list at O(n) cost, and up to n-1 pops can occur, so the merge phase dominates at O(n^2). An O(n log n) version exists: ||build a separate output list, appending each interval and only extending the last output interval's end when it overlaps||. Space is O(n) only because of Timsort's auxiliary storage; the merge itself is in-place. Minor style: `key=lambda x: x[0]` can be written `key=itemgetter(0)` or dropped entirely, since the default list comparison already sorts by start then end.
complexity.summary: Sorts intervals by start, then merges in place: whenever the next interval overlaps the current one it extends the current end and removes the next interval with pop(i+1), otherwise advances.
